metaDescription: Licensed electrician in Wellington, FL. Panel upgrades, generator hookups, and pool electrical for the equestrian suburb, day or night. Book a visit.
intro: Wellington is an equestrian suburb of larger lots, pools, and homes built mostly from the 1970s onward. The equipment here runs newer, but bigger properties carry heavier loads, and generators are now standard storm prep. When a panel cannot keep up, a pool needs bonding, or a generator needs a proper transfer switch, our licensed crew plans it right the first time.
housingNotes: Wellington's housing leans newer than most cities we serve, built out largely from the 1970s onward around its equestrian roots. Properties run larger, with more acreage, pools, and outbuildings, so the service often carries more load than the original panel was sized for. Generators are common here, and one installed without the right transfer switch adds risk. Pools are near standard, so bonding and grounding matter as much as anywhere.
permitNote: In Wellington, service changes, generator installations, and pool electrical corrections are permitted work through the village building department under the Florida Building Code. Ghost Crown Electric pulls the permit in our own name, schedules the inspection, and our licensed crew meets the inspector in person, so the work is documented and signed off correctly.

challenges.heading: Larger properties with growing electrical loads
challenges.body: Wellington's lots run larger than typical, often with barns, outbuildings, and pools added over time. The original panel was not always sized for everything that got plugged into it. We assess the whole property, not just the main house, before forecasting the work.

challenges.heading: Generators without proper transfer switches
challenges.body: Storm season makes reliable power essential, and many Wellington households run generators. One installed without a correctly permitted transfer switch can backfeed the grid or damage equipment. Our licensed crew installs and inspects generator hookups the way the code requires.

challenges.heading: Pools on larger properties
challenges.body: Pools are near standard across Wellington properties, and the bonding and grounding around them can loosen or corrode over the years. A yearly pool electrical inspection, ideally before heater season, catches those issues before they become a safety problem for your family.

faqs.question: Do you serve Wellington day or night?
faqs.answer: Yes. We run north into Palm Beach County regularly, and Wellington is a steady part of that coverage. We answer the phone whenever you call, day or night, and you reach a licensed electrician, not a call center.

faqs.question: Can you install a generator with a proper transfer switch?
faqs.answer: Yes. We assess your panel and your property's load, size the transfer switch correctly, pull the permit in our own name, and meet the inspector in person. A generator installed without the right transfer switch can backfeed the grid or damage equipment, so it is not a step worth skipping.

faqs.question: My property has grown over the years. Can my panel keep up?
faqs.answer: It depends on what has been added since the panel was sized, since barns, pools, outbuildings, and larger equipment all add load. We assess the property as it stands today, not just the main house, and give you an honest read on whether the panel needs an upgrade.
